[@Shankar Warang](/edgeware/account/jA7pLH65zgRNA4UgwqHEWWRxTgg51wuAUgfzmZoYWM2dMVS) sorry just seeing these.

> Rich was very vocal about not letting the agency take any credits for Kabocha even though many of the agency members helped Kabocha many times.

I don't agree - I worked with Thom to ensure the agency was positioned as the group who created the 'RFP' to which Kabocha was a response. If you check back, you'll see this framing. 

There has always been credit given to those who helped - as far as im aware, on specifics, the financial team gave some recommends on crowdloan incentives and a spreadsheet that outlined returns from other projects. These were credited in discussion threads.

Aside from that, agency team members were recruited - like Jan/Johan to develop the crowdloan UI. This is separate from the agency... 

Please let me know if i'm missing anything?

> Rich also mentioned that Filip showed up in the community by himself and thus agency shouldn't take credit for that even though agency members helped him with the onboarding process and follow-ups. By this logic, didn't rusty crewmates show up in the community by themselves?

We have a lot of people appear in discord / telegram - it takes a lot of time to sift through to those who add value. I do this a lot and never mention, but Filip turned out to be useful and qualifed and a good cultural fit. 

I spent this time, and organised things, my point back then was that the agency taking credit for bringing the EVM to edgeware was a little misleading. I stand by that, given the agency were not directly involved in recruiting the talent who has delivered the work.

Again - let me know if I've missed something.

body:
> I do think the delivered and ongoing items should be linked with more clarity. Repositories for code products like the palletes etc. We do want to make sure we're not being double-dipped on these things, and clear scopes help that. 
 
Definitely, see my above note to [@kosturp](/edgeware/account/nooQF75e7yWJk5QMkd67t8bgW9R58tpu6zdKcuhHCbK1dg6) - the proposal was rushed on-chain and so all of these issues should have not occured. 

> Because this proposal text seems to be pretty rough (Something an NSP should review and resolve.. ) it's not entirely clear that this applies, however I'll state that : 

Agree. 

> The norm of proposing payment for unscoped work after the fact versus getting community consensus on a scope prior is a risky one. Proposal-makers should not be surprised or offended if the community tries to negotiate deliverables it hadn't agreed to. 

> The risk is inherent, and the burden falls on the proposal-maker and their NSF to prove the work is of value and to quality. I believe we all want to receive proposals like this in good faith, and very often we do recognize the value delivered, but proposal-makers should also be ready to describe and argue the value of the work if they choose the retro- path. 

Agree - the onus is on the proposal maker / NSP to make the case, since EDG holders are the group that votes to fund. 

It seems there was enough good will this time to balance the lack of clarity.

I don't really have any issue with the amounts at play here given the deliverables described.


I do think the delivered and ongoing items should be linked with more clarity. Repositories for code products like the palletes etc. We do want to make sure we're not being double-dipped on these things, and clear scopes help that. 


Because this proposal text seems to be pretty rough (Something an NSP should review and resolve.. ) it's not entirely clear that this applies, however I'll state that : 

The norm of proposing payment for unscoped work after the fact versus getting community consensus on a scope prior is a risky one. Proposal-makers should not be surprised or offended if the community tries to negotiate deliverables it hadn't agreed to.  

The risk is inherent, and the burden falls on the proposal-maker and their NSF to prove the work is of value and to quality.  I believe we all want to receive proposals like this in good faith, and very often we do recognize the value delivered, but proposal-makers should also be ready to describe and argue the value of the work if they choose the retro- path.

Don't get me wrong, no one is signaling downvote for you, I'm a fan of your work on Kabocha and I'm not planning to vote against the proposal...I just walked through the old and new proposal from a high level, highlighted things I was missing there. I'm good with your additional explanation.

Sorry been away with the family so trying to take a break.

I agree the proposal could/should have been clearer - honestly, it was rushed for various reasons, and I knew at the time that we would need to explain more, but given the amount ramsey has contributed, I felt it was ok to push to voting.

With hindsight I'd have held off until things were much clearer and this request was defined in relation to other funded grants - lesson learned.

agree with Shankar on this one. The original thread which is covering some topics (edgeware-road-parachains-and-bridges-core-development) is missing updates and this one does not include work evaluation draft.

Milestone 1 was done once Kabocha was launched. -  April 2022

Edgeware Road - I left update there, that has been done a long time ago. I am not sure why we are bringing up things like this, in order to signal a downvote for the value of Ramsey(Decentration). 

Since Milestone 1 was completed more than a month ago, I have been working almost every day 10 hours a day, sometimes 7 days. If we want to work out by hourly. My hourly is $150 to $250 (or more) per hour. 50 hours a week is >$30k a month, i have charged far less than that at 5m EDG for 5 weeks.

> Edgeware RoadParachain, relay and bridge research 
> Done

On this, I nudged [@Decentration](/edgeware/account/mHDNswFgLQiiXGwkWCXgpwE27eppYppa96cMNWzT2kQF27z) to update his [original proposal](https://gov.edgewa.re/discussion/1327-edgeware-road-parachains-and-bridges-core-development) for Edgeware road.

see comment above - the challenge is everyone invoices / charges / values things in a different way - we have very little standardisation a yet, so its left for individuals / teams to make a case. 

Ramsey chooses to invoice in EDG - no USD/fiat equivalent, which is his choice.

It's totally fine to invoice in EDG if you publish a framework draft supporting the evaluation of any work in EDG.
As of now, we do have a well-tested standard structure/framework set up for the evaluation in USD as well as the periodic incentives of contributors.

No - this funding is for previous and ongoing work in EDG primarily - that could be clearer, there's just a lot of stuff that has been happening on that front and we have a clearer connection now between EDG/KAB from a technical, cultural, value exchange perspective. 

I'll let [@Decentration](/edgeware/account/mHDNswFgLQiiXGwkWCXgpwE27eppYppa96cMNWzT2kQF27z) share his perspective too.
Then sorry but this proposal doesn't make sense at all. Almost all the items mentioned are already covered in several other proposals funded or being funded.

Appreciate the comment, this post was translated from an invoice ramsey created - you can [view it here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gHiR2Pl8YiuZDnEAIOA6CeRCLaVphbfwO5YZcKnoZgE/edit)

The document lay out there, may make it a little easier to view. 

There is a whole heap of work that is ongoing on Ramsey's side - so think of this as a catchall for that work billed in EDG (not USD).

If you want to work backwards this is around £10,000, which is not a lot, given it covers a few months of time.

There is no doubt Ramsey is worth this given his work across the project - not including the work on Kabocha / Parachain and Bridges.

-----

*** Onboarding dev teams into Edgeware**
    * Rusty Crewmates (Timothee, charles and Nathan)
    * The time taken to do this and value add here should not be underestimated.
    * They have already completed one new pallet project and are working on two more via the Task Team propossls.

*** Pallet (Dorg)**
* multisig improvements for Edgeware, Kabocha and all Substrate Chains
* This is currently in review with W3F and will likely receive a grant and also be adopted across other substrate chains.

* Making Edgeware more constructive and process oriented on the developer front.

*** Guide on upgrade strategy (unblocking)**
* Advising / working with Flipchan, advice was to split upgrade into two parts.

The proposal outline could have been clearer, so I take responsibility for that since I put it to the chain.

After milestone 1 completed:

Playing the role of:
- engineer,
- pallet designer/architect
- product manager
- product developer,
- steward for both edgeware and kabocha, work more than full time, creating community
- developing relations with outside stakeholders
- helping to coordinate development
- startup duties outside the role of technical steward maintainer.
- creative director


There are many who support Ramsey(Decentration) and the value that I provide for the eco-system, and be willing to pay very reasonable and fair remuneration for such value. 

> Rich was very vocal about not letting the agency take any credits for Kabocha even though many of the agency members helped Kabocha many times.
> Rich also mentioned that Filip showed up in the community by himself and thus agency shouldn't take credit for that even though agency members helped him with the onboarding process and follow-ups. By this logic, didn't rusty crewmates show up in the community by themselves?
Reading your comments i think this is personal for you, and also making a tit-for-tat war with Edgeware Agency and Decent Partners. I am not going to get sucked into this. 

I have established my values, honour and good faith. By having to justify them again is a bit insulting for me. The amount seems to have triggered you (which is well within the median range of market value), so its not a constructuve conversation.

People should be paid what they're willing to negotiate and bargain for.

I am also not a fan of unions. We're here to design better systems, not fall into same traps as before.
Also, please add the calculations/explanation for the 5.03M EDG value.
Will this be considered as one of the parts of Kabocha Steward's milestone 2?
